requirement: Requirement and reference names MUST have nonempty dot-separated segments containing only ASCII letters, digits, underscores, or hyphens. A `{req}` directive whose full name is invalid, including one whose chapter path gives an invalid namespace, and a role with an invalid name MUST remain literal and MUST NOT define or reference a requirement. For nested chapter paths, a leading `reqs/` and a final `index` or `README` segment MUST be omitted from the requirement namespace.
rationale:
I found no gaps. Each obligation has an implementing item and a test that asserts its outcome.

**1. Names have nonempty dot-separated segments of ASCII letters, digits, `_` or `-`.**
- `valid_name` (src/lib.rs) enforces this. The name must be nonempty, and every `.`-split part must be nonempty and made only of ASCII alphanumerics, `_` or `-`.
- Test: `invalid_names_remain_literal` covers the empty name, `a..b`, `.a`, `a.`, `a b`, `café`, `a/b`, `a&b` and `` a`b ``. It also covers the valid cases `a`, `a_b.c-d`, `A1.b2` and `x.-_.y`.

**2. A `{req}` directive with an invalid full name stays literal and defines nothing.**
- The local name is checked first. `definition_blocks` (src/lib.rs) only recognizes a block whose local name is valid or built-in.
- The full name is checked next, using the chapter namespace from `full_requirement_name`.
  - `replace_definitions` filters on `valid_name(full name)`, so an invalid full name stays literal in the book.
  - `preprocess_book` skips such a directive, so it defines nothing.
  - `collect_definitions` (src/evidence.rs) reports "invalid requirement name", sets `named = false` and `continue`s before inserting, so nothing is defined.
- Tests:
  - `invalid_names_remain_literal` checks `:::{req} bad name` stays literal, and that a valid local name in the invalid namespace `a&b` leaves the source unchanged.
  - `chapters_with_invalid_namespaces_define_nothing_in_the_book` runs `preprocess_book` on `bad dir/rules.md` and checks the content is unchanged, no badge is added, no detail page is generated, and the reference `bad dir.rules.good` stays literal.
  - `invalid_full_names_from_chapter_paths_are_reported_and_not_defined` (src/evidence.rs) checks the validator reports the error and defines nothing.

**3. A role with an invalid name stays literal and references nothing.**
- `reference_roles` (src/lib.rs) pushes a match only if `valid_name(name)` or the name is built-in.
- `opening_fence` (src/fenced.rs) applies the same check to fenced roles.
- Tests:
  - `invalid_names_remain_literal` runs `reference_roles` over `impl`, `cite`, `test` and `term` with invalid names, in both markdown and non-markdown modes.
  - `opening_fences_take_a_role_and_one_valid_or_built_in_name` checks that `a b`, `a..b`, `.a`, `a.`, `a/b`, `café.b` and others return `None`.

**4. For nested chapter paths, a leading `reqs/` and a final `index` or `README` segment are omitted.**
- `chapter_namespace` (src/lib.rs) does this only when the path has more than one component.
- Test: `chapter_path_prefixes_the_requirement_name` covers `reqs/foo/bar`, `reqs/foo/README`, `reqs/foo/index`, `foo/index`, `reqs/index` (empty namespace), `reqs/bar`, the non-nested `index` and `reqs`, and `other/reqs/a`.
- The evidence-side tests also run this logic: `validates_full_names_requirement_text_and_input_lines` and the `reqs/index.md` case in `invalid_full_names_from_chapter_paths_are_reported_and_not_defined`.

**Marking and unspecified behavior.**
- The other `definition_blocks` callers I read are `declaration_line_ranges` and `marker_ranges`, plus `direct_references`, which scans text it has already extracted. They do not bypass the name checks.
- The error reporting in `collect_definitions` is covered by the `requirements.ci.definition_errors` {impl} reference on the same item, so I do not count it as unspecified behavior.
